items: YAML (YAML Ain’t Markup Language): A human-readable data format used to describe hierarchical data. YAML is a superset of JSON and is often used for configuration files due to its clean syntax.
Spring Profile: A Spring Boot feature that allows developers to define environment-specific configurations (like dev, test, prod), so the application can behave differently based on the environment.

application.yml File: A YAML-based configuration file used in Spring Boot as an alternative to application.properties. It allows defining all environment-specific settings in one structured file using sections separated by ---.
-- in YAML: Indicates the beginning of a new document. Used to define different profile-specific configuration blocks within a single YAML file.
Combines all profile configurations in one file.
Reduces redundancy.
More readable and structured compared to .properties.
Automatically supported in Spring Boot (via SnakeYAML parser).
Open Spring Tool Suite (STS).
Import the project: InfyGoBoot_Profiles from Demo 7.
Rename it to: InfyGoBoot_YAML.
Delete all application.properties files.
Create a new file: application.yml in src/main/resources.

content.code:
# Default properties and active profile
spring:
  profiles:
    active: dev

  mvc:
    view:
      prefix: /WEB-INF/pages/
      suffix: .jsp

server:
  servlet:
    context-path: /InfyGoBoot
  port: 4343

logging:
  file: Errorlog.log
  level:
    root: warn
    com.infosys.ars: error
  pattern:
    file: "%d{yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss,SSS} %5p [%t] %c [%M] - %m%n"

---
# Development profile properties
spring:
  profiles: dev
  datasource:
    url: jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/db_irs
    username: root
    password: root
  jpa:
    show-sql: true

---
# Test profile properties
spring:
  profiles: test
  datasource:
    url: jdbc:hsqldb:mem:scratchdb/db_irs
    username: sa
    password:
  jpa:
    show-sql: true

sections.heading: How Profile Documents Work in YAML

items: You can define shared/default configurations and override specific values in profile sections using ---.

content.code:
# Shared config (no profile)
spring:
  datasource:
    username: root
    password: root

---
spring:
  profiles: dev
  datasource:
    url: jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/db_irs_dev

---
spring:
  profiles: test
  datasource:
    url: jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/db_irs_test

items: If dev is active: url = db_irs_dev
If test is active: url = db_irs_test
If no profile is active: url = undefined, but username and password still apply.
Spring Boot uses the SnakeYAML parser.
No extra setup needed—YAML is automatically supported via spring-boot-starter.
YAML is a powerful alternative to .properties.
Enables a single unified configuration file for multiple environments.
Improves readability and maintainability.
Profiles in YAML are separated by -- and loaded based on the spring.profiles.active key.
